curation.system_role: A procurement-facing shell that bridged a public port authority to an offshore advisory service.
curation.lead: Harbor Ledger Holdings LLC is the core shell in the portfolio demo. A Florida filing [REG:FL:L23000214567] puts the entity on paper, a hosted board-minute excerpt [HARBOR-LEDGER-BOARD-MINUTES-2024-11] shows directors approving a sensitive services addendum, and an internal source record [PORT-WATCH-CALL-NOTES-2025-02-14] explains why the deal was routed through an intermediary rather than through the authority's normal vendor channel.

sections.title: Why It Matters
sections.content: The company was formed just before the procurement shortlist and then described as a "local implementation partner" despite no public operating footprint [Finding #9001, #9004]. That combination is not proof of misconduct, but it is exactly the pattern investigative tooling should make legible.

sections.title: Control Signals
sections.content: The strongest public control signal is not the Florida filing itself but the combination of the hosted minutes and the UK advisory record [HARBOR-LEDGER-BOARD-MINUTES-2024-11][REG:UK:12345678]. The source-record path matters here because some corroboration is inspectable and some is not [Finding #9002, #9003].

sections.title: Audit Trail
sections.content: The procurement packet shows Harbor Ledger entering the narrative as a local delivery vehicle [DOCUMENTCLOUD:24402693]. The demo article treats that packet, the board minutes, and the metadata-only interview memo as different evidence classes rather than flattening them into one confidence bucket [Finding #9004, #9005].

open_questions: Who controlled Estuary Advisory's beneficial interest at the moment Harbor Ledger was shortlisted?
Was Meridian Port Authority aware that Lina Ortega attended Harbor Ledger governance calls as an observer?

findings.summary: Harbor Ledger was formed in Florida eleven days before Meridian Port Authority finalized its implementation shortlist.
findings.detail: The filing timing places the entity inside the key procurement window and makes it a useful demo case for timing, provenance, and shell-pattern analysis.
